usage.result_excerpt:
I wrote the solution in `main.wj`. I ran only Example 2 (the five-line input). It produced the expected output, `0 none`, `0 none`, `1 2`, `2 3`, `25 97`. I didn't run Example 1 or test the upper bound of 200000.

The program sieves primes up to 200000 once. It then builds a prefix count and the largest prime at or below each value, so every query is a table lookup. Any `n` below 2 prints `0 none`
